svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Genomes differ in size and in sequence."], [1, "Genome size varies enormously, and does not match complexity."], [7.5, "Within a species, genomes are almost identical..."], [10, "...between species, the differences are much larger."]]
svg.title: Genome size and diversity
svg.desc: Logarithmic bar chart of genome sizes from E. coli to the plant Paris japonica, with comparisons of base sequence similarity within humans and between humans and chimpanzees.

g.data-info: Total DNA per genome, in millions of base pairs (Mb): E. coli 4.6, yeast 12, fruit fly ~140, human ~3 100, onion ~16 000, Paris japonica (a plant) ~149 000.
g.text: genome size / million base pairs (log scale)

g.data-info: Any two humans share about 99.9% of their base sequence.
Humans and chimpanzees differ in about 1–2% of base sequence; more distant species differ far more.
